knowledge_gaps: Equal residual weights do not imply equally tuned controls: sparse transition scores and dense popularity scores have different distributions despite percentile normalization. The proposed weights may barely affect transition rankings; report component score differences and ranking changes before interpreting a negative result.

Reproducibility requires the calibration sample size, prefix sampling distribution, history truncation, evaluation mode, numerical degeneracy threshold, and percentile convention. Clarify that one branch and weight are selected jointly across all four categories.

Training-derived transition tables contain the pairs scored by training diagnostics. Such measurements describe fit and can overstate generalization; separate them from validation evidence and consider leave-user-out transition diagnostics.

A popularity comparison alone cannot isolate directional or recency information. Reverse-transition, last-item-only, or degree-preserving shuffled controls would strengthen interpretation, but should enter a separately budgeted follow-up.

The report leaves checkpoint selection and host evaluation orchestration unspecified. Predeclare the checkpoint schedule, five fusion configurations, evaluation costs, stopping rule, and exploratory paired uncertainty where host outputs permit it. Validation selection across previous attempts also contributes to overfitting.

Fused diagnostics need an explicit history-aware scoring hook because predict_score(features, items) cannot reconstruct transition scores from neural features alone. Verify routing, zero-weight ranking equivalence, candidate-order invariance, and chunked versus unchunked prediction parity.

Originality 3 is reasonable; potential 7 remains speculative without validation or coverage results. Difficulty 3 understates coordinated diagnostic and predictor changes; 4 is more defensible. Verify the cited transition study's exact algorithm and experiments before relying on its summary.
